You think you've explored medicine. In reality, you're standing in the parking lot of Disney World bragging about how fun the pavement is. You've taken pictures of the asphalt. You've written dissertations about the parking stripes. You've never gone inside.

After a century of pharmacology, most beneficial effects of molecules on diseases remain unexplored. Not because biology is constrained. Because clinical trials are slow, expensive, and run by people who think "urgency" is a type of perfume.

Here's the math. It's painful but brief, like a flu shot administered by someone who hates you.

## Your Tiny Sandbox

Here is everything humanity considers "medicine" after 5,000 years of civilization:

* **Prescriptions:** {{< var fda_approved_products_count >}} approved in the U.S. Sounds impressive until you realize most are just "Tylenol, but blue."
* **Unique Ingredients:** These products contain only {{< var fda_approved_unique_active_ingredients >}}. Fewer ingredients than a decent French bakery uses.
* **Investigational Drugs:** {{< var phase_1_passed_compounds_global >}} have passed Phase I globally. Progress!
* **Safe Stuff:** The FDA GRAS list contains {{< var fda_gras_substances_count >}}. These are things you could eat right now without dying. Low bar. Still useful.

**Total unique compounds humanity knows are safe-ish: {{< var safe_compounds_count >}}.**

That's it. That's your entire medicine cabinet after five millennia.

## The Target List (Ways Your Body Breaks)

* **Codes:** The ICD-10 lists {{< var icd_10_total_codes_nounit >}} ways your meat can malfunction. Humanity's most comprehensive to-do list, and you're ignoring it.
* **Real Targets:** After consolidation, {{< var trial_relevant_diseases_count >}} trial-relevant diseases worth actually fixing.

![Fourteen thousand ways to be sick, but only 1,000 worth testing drugs against. The other 13,000 are just spelling variations.](/assets/images/untapped-therapeutic-frontier/untapped-therapeutic-frontier-section-the-target-list-ways-your-body-breaks-bw-academic.jpg)

## The Math You're Ignoring

Take your {{< var safe_compounds_count >}} safe compounds. Multiply by {{< var trial_relevant_diseases_count >}}. This gives you the "Combinatorial Space," which is fancy talk for "stuff you could test tomorrow if you weren't busy filling out forms."

**{{< var safe_compounds_count >}} × {{< var trial_relevant_diseases_count >}} = {{< var drug_disease_combinations_possible >}} plausible drug-condition combinations.**

### What You've Actually Tested

* **Approved uses:** {{< var approved_drug_disease_pairings >}} unique approved drug-disease pairings. Your entire medical canon.
* **Repurposed uses:** {{< var drug_repurposing_success_rate >}} of drugs gain at least one new indication after initial approval. The rest never get a second date.
* **Failed trials:** Let's be generous and say you tested 10x as many things that failed. (You did. You learned nothing from them.)

![Most drug trials fail. A few succeed. Humanity's entire medical knowledge is a tiny pile of successes next to a mountain of expensive failures we learned nothing from.](/assets/images/untapped-therapeutic-frontier/untapped-therapeutic-frontier-section-what-you-ve-actually-tested-bw-academic.jpg)

**Total tested: {{< var tested_relationships_estimate >}}.**

### The Scorecard

{{< var tested_relationships_estimate >}} tested / {{< var drug_disease_combinations_possible >}} possibilities = {{< var exploration_ratio >}}

{{< var exploration_ratio_latex >}}

**Humanity has explored about a third of one percent of the theoretically testable drug-disease space.**

You are the detective who searched one drawer and declared the case cold.

![The dot is everything you know about medicine. The rest is everything you don't. The dot is very small. You seem comfortable with this.](/assets/images/untapped-therapeutic-frontier/untapped-therapeutic-frontier-section-the-scorecard-bw-academic.jpg)

It's like reading the first page of *War and Peace* and writing a book report called "It's About a Party." Technically accurate. Cosmically insufficient.

## Is The Untested Stuff Useful?

You might argue, "Maybe the other {{< var unexplored_ratio >}} is useless!"

![You've figured out 12 percent of how the body works. The other 88 percent is a mystery. Drugs affect multiple pathways at once. You test them on one pathway at a time.](/assets/images/untapped-therapeutic-frontier/untapped-therapeutic-frontier-section-is-the-untested-stuff-useful-bw-academic.jpg)

Biology would like a word.

* **Undrugged Targets:** Mapping 350,000+ clinical trials showed that only {{< var human_interactome_targeted_pct >}} of the human interactome has ever been targeted by drugs. You're ignoring 88% of your own biology. It's like having a 100-room mansion and living exclusively in the bathroom.
* **Polypharmacology:** Drugs are messy. They hit multiple targets. FDA-approved drugs often bind to things you didn't intend. This means "side effects" are frequently "cures for something else" that nobody bothered to notice. Sildenafil was developed for chest pain. It failed. Its "side effect" became Viagra, then got repurposed *again* for pulmonary hypertension. Minoxidil was developed for high blood pressure. Its "side effect" was growing hair. It became Rogaine. Two drugs. Three accidental cures. Zero systematic searches. You keep finding cures by tripping over them in hallways. Imagine if you opened a door on purpose.
* **Network Overlap:** Diseases cluster on shared biological networks [@disease-network-overlap]. Arthritis and Alzheimer's share biological pathways. Lithium was prescribed for gout in the 1800s; decades later, it turned out to be the gold standard treatment for bipolar disorder. Nobody connected the dots because nobody was drawing lines between diseases. The drug that treats your grandfather's inflammation might fix your grandmother's neurodegeneration. You won't find out, because testing it would require paperwork that takes longer than Grandma has left.

## The Universe is Big. You Are Small.

So far we only counted molecules humanity *already has*. The stuff in your cupboards. If you look at what's chemically possible, it gets embarrassing.

![All the molecules you've discovered are a grain of sand. All the molecules that could exist are the planet Earth. You're very proud of your grain of sand.](/assets/images/untapped-therapeutic-frontier/untapped-therapeutic-frontier-section-the-universe-is-big-you-are-small-bw-academic.jpg)

* **Chemical Space:** Estimated 10^23 to 10^60\ [@chemical-space-size] drug-like molecules. That's more candidates than there are atoms in your body. Or stars in the galaxy. Or excuses from your regulatory agencies.
* **Virtual Libraries:** ZINC-22 contains tens of billions [@zinc-22-database] of purchasable virtual molecules. You could order them online. You haven't.
* **Synthesized:** You have made **<10^(-40)** of possible molecules.

**Tested / Possible = ~10^-20 to 10^-50.**

**Effectively zero.** You haven't even started.

This is like exploring Earth by looking at one grain of sand on one beach in New Jersey, then declaring you've "seen the world." You haven't. You've seen a grain of sand. In New Jersey.

## Why You Are Still Sick

It's not because science is hard. It's because you've built a system that is allergic to answers.

1. **Trials Cost Too Much:** A typical Phase II-III RCT costs **$30-$100M** (Median cost per patient {{< var traditional_phase3_cost_per_patient >}}). At that price, you only test "sure things." Safe bets. Boring bets. Bets that don't cure cancer. Clinical trials are a velvet-rope nightclub where the bouncer is a regulatory agency and the cover charge is a hundred million dollars.

![High costs, patent rules, and fear of lawsuits form a bottleneck between cures and people. The bottleneck is shaped like a dollar sign.](/assets/images/untapped-therapeutic-frontier/untapped-therapeutic-frontier-section-why-you-are-still-sick-bw-academic.jpg)

2. **Herd Mentality:** Trials overwhelmingly test the same few biological targets due to preferential attachment dynamics [@preferential-target-attachment]. Everyone studies what everyone else studies because that's how you get grants. It's like if every explorer only went to France because France already had good reviews on TripAdvisor. Meanwhile, undiscovered continents full of cures sit there, undiscovered.

3. **No Profit:** Most molecules have no patent. No patent = no $100M trial = no approval. Metformin, a diabetes drug from the 1950s, shows persistent signals for reducing cancer risk and extending lifespan. It costs pennies. It's off-patent. The trial to prove it works for aging (TAME) spent years begging for funding because no pharmaceutical company will bankroll a drug they can't monopolize. The molecule that saves your life has to make money first. If it can't, it won't. You die. Quarterly earnings go up.

4. **Neglect:** If you have a rare disease with no market, you don't get a drug. Your cells malfunction in an unprofitable way. The invisible hand of the market has weighed your life against quarterly earnings and found you wanting. Sorry about your death. It was a business decision.

## How Long to Explore Everything?

At the current pace of {{< var current_trials_per_year >}}, how long would it take to systematically test therapeutic possibilities?

### Tier 1: Single Compounds (Most Conservative)

Testing every known safe compound against every major disease:

**{{< var drug_disease_combinations_possible >}} ÷ {{< var current_trials_per_year >}} = {{< var current_known_safe_exploration_years >}}**

That's almost {{< var current_known_safe_exploration_years >}} to explore compounds we *already know are safe*. By that math, we won't finish until the year 5000.

### Tier 2: Combination Therapies (Still Defensible)

Modern medicine increasingly relies on multi-drug cocktails. Oncology, HIV, cardiology, psychiatry: all routinely use drug combinations. So the real question isn't "does this one drug work?" It's "which combinations work?" Testing pairwise combinations of safe compounds:

**{{< var combination_therapy_disease_space >}} ÷ {{< var current_trials_per_year >}} = {{< var current_combination_exploration_years >}}**

That's longer than *Homo sapiens* has existed as a species. And that's using only compounds with established safety data, testing only pairs. Not triplets. God help you if you want to try triplets.

![Testing every two-drug combination would take millions of years. You have about 70 years if you're lucky. The math is not in your favor.](/assets/images/untapped-therapeutic-frontier/untapped-therapeutic-frontier-section-tier-2-combination-therapies-still-defensible-bw-academic.jpg)

### Tier 3: The Full Chemical Universe (Illustrative)

Beyond known compounds lies the chemical space of 10^23 to 10^60 drug-like molecules. At current trial capacity, exploring even the *synthesizable* fraction would take longer than the universe has existed. The universe is 13.8 billion years old. You need more time than that. To test pills. Pills that already exist.

We haven't even started.

### "But Won't We Run Out of Easy Discoveries?"

Some will argue "diminishing returns": the more we search, the harder each new discovery becomes. This assumes we've already picked the low-hanging fruit.

We haven't picked *any* fruit. We're still in the parking lot arguing about whether fruit exists.

Diminishing returns only kicks in after you've explored a significant fraction of the space. At <1% explored, every trial teaches you something new about human biology, improving your ability to predict what works next. Learning compounds. Depletion is negligible. You are nowhere near the bottom of the barrel because you have not yet located the barrel.

The math: even with weak learning, diminishing returns only matters after exploring ~37% of therapeutic space. For combination therapies, that crossover is **over 5 million years away** at current pace (37% of {{< var combination_therapy_disease_space_nounit >}} combinations at {{< var current_trials_per_year_nounit >}} trials/year).

You cannot have diminishing returns when you've barely started looking. See [the formal analysis](https://impact.warondisease.org#mathematical-framework-when-would-diminishing-returns-dominate) for the equations.

## The Fix

The Oxford RECOVERY Trial (COVID-19) proved that large-scale pragmatic trials can run for ~{{< var recovery_trial_cost_per_patient >}} and deliver results in <100 days [@recovery-trial-100-days-to-cure].

{{< var recovery_trial_cost_per_patient >}} vs {{< var traditional_phase3_cost_per_patient >}}. Read those numbers again. One of them is the reason people are dying.

With a [decentralized FDA](../solution/dfda.qmd), trial capacity increases by {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_multiplier >}}:

**{{< var drug_disease_combinations_possible >}} ÷ {{< var dfda_trials_per_year_capacity >}} = {{< var dfda_known_safe_exploration_years >}}**

Still a long time, but at least it's a number with fewer digits than a phone book. And the first few decades would capture the highest-value discoveries (the low-hanging fruit that current trial scarcity forces you to ignore while people die in the waiting room).

More importantly, your decentralized FDA builds *permanent infrastructure* for systematic therapeutic exploration. The goal isn't to "finish." It's to stop leaving cures on the table while you form subcommittees to discuss whether to form committees to review the proposal to consider them.

![Traditional trials: expensive, slow, picky about participants. Decentralized trials: cheaper, faster, will accept literally anyone. Both test the same drugs.](/assets/images/untapped-therapeutic-frontier/untapped-therapeutic-frontier-section-the-fix-pragmatic-vs-traditional-bw-academic.jpg)

## The Bottom Line

**Humanity has empirically tested less than {{< var exploration_ratio >}} of the drug-disease relationships that can be tested using existing safe compounds.**

**If you include the larger chemical universe, humanity has explored roughly one-quadrillionth to one-quintillionth of what is possible (10^-12 to 10^-50). There are numbers so small that mathematicians get depressed looking at them. These are those numbers.**

**The overwhelming majority of therapeutic potential remains untouched. Not because cures are impossible. Because trials are too expensive and too slow.**

**A decentralized, automated pragmatic trial system is the only route to systematically explore the remaining 99.999...% of medical space.**

You're not in the parking lot because there's nothing inside Disney World. You're in the parking lot because the entrance fee is $100 million and requires 17 years of paperwork. People are dying in the parking lot. The rides are right there. You can hear the screaming. (Fun screaming. Cure screaming.)

![Everything you know about medicine is a dot. Everything you could know is the universe. Between them: money and time. You have neither.](/assets/images/untapped-therapeutic-frontier/untapped-therapeutic-frontier-section-the-bottom-line-bw-academic.jpg)

The cures are inside. Open the gate.
